scope.repair_scope: Entire boundary node reread; exact weak-L2 definition, orthonormality, finite projection identity and constant-one test newly derived.

findings: Re-read the entire revised boundary node. In the real space L2(0,2pi), weak convergence to zero is explicitly defined by the integral against every real L2 test function, using the stated unnormalized dx inner product.
Reproduced orthonormality of e_n=sin(nx)/sqrt(pi) from 2 sin(nx) sin(mx)=cos((n-m)x)-cos((n+m)x): the integral is zero for n!=m and pi for n=m. No completeness assertion is used.

For arbitrary fixed g, expanded the squared norm of g minus the first N coefficients: ||g||^2-2 sum a_n^2+sum a_n^2. Nonnegativity bounds every partial sum of squared coefficients; hence a_n tends to zero, giving every required weak test for sin(nx).
The squared functions and the constant test 1 lie in L2 of this finite interval. Their pairing is pi for every n, so the same definition rules out weak convergence of the squares to zero.

The margin, endpoint-exponent and translated-bump models are unchanged and were re-read for scope. The new proof supplies an omitted explanation in a separate boundary example; it is not an input needed to pass the strong Holder-limit equation.
